Stay in a Real Castle | Augill Castle, Cumbria & the Dales
Skip to content
Augill Castle is a 19th century castle nestled between the Yorkshire Dales and Cumbria’s Lake District.
Dedicated to comfort, friendliness and informality, traveller-rated five star Augill Castle offers you the two most elusive luxuries of modern life – quality space and time together.
In short, we’re a place where you can be your best self.
FIND OUT MORE
Explore
Eat, drink and sleep at Augill Castle Hotel & Restaurant, the north of England’s best castle stay.
It’s twenty five years since we stepped through the front door of Augill and we’re as excited now as we were then to share the castle with you.
We’ve all got a lot on our minds and in a world where life feels crazier than ever the castle is a rare sanctuary of calm and mild eccentricity.
Get away from it all, stay in a castle and re-discover what living is all about.

Castle Stays UK | Rooms & Suites at Augill Castle, Cumbria
Skip to content
Sleep in a Castle
Augill Castle is a truly unique and wonderful place to stay where you can cocoon yourself or strike out and explore England’s two most popular national parks on our doorstep.
While the world has changed the fundamentals of what makes a stay in one of our bedrooms or suites hasn’t.
Beautiful, quirky rooms
Big comfy beds
Dreamy linen
Deep baths and decent showers
Huge towels and fluffy bathrobes
Our Rooms
Nestled in the heart of the Eden Valley, our 19th-century castle offers a unique blend of historic elegance and modern amenities. Each room is individually designed with antique furnishings, luxurious fabrics, and many have views of the surrounding countryside.
Whether you and your guests are staying in a cosy garden suite or one of our grand bedrooms, you’ll find thoughtful touches that ensure a memorable stay. Relax in the tranquility of our peaceful retreat and let the timeless ambiance of Augill Castle transport you to a world of comfort and relaxation. pages.text:
About Augill Castle | A 19th-Century Castle in Cumbria
Skip to content
About Augill Castle
Does Augill dance to your beat?
We certainly hope so
but choosing somewhere to stay is more difficult than ever - there’s just so much choice.
Augill Castle may be unlike anywhere you have ever stayed before. Why? It is, as one guest wrote, perfectly imperfect. The castle has been our family home for twenty four years and we seek to recreate a slice of our life here for you. We aren t trying to be a luxury hotel which strives to create order out of chaos, rather to celebrate with like-minded people the fact that life is chaotic and we re all in it together.
And as for that beat; it changes with the seasons. The castle is a very different place during school holidays when families fill the place and if you are lucky enough to find yourself here on a quiet night midweek you may find you can create your own music.
"I feel like we've been in a perfect little bubble for the last two days. All the brilliant little touches aside, it's like there is a spell over the castle, the atmosphere is wonderful and I don't know how you do that.. it's magic!"
When we bought the castle in 1997 we started with three bedrooms, our guests sharing our family home with us, eating together, sharing the same space and enjoying a shared genuine country house experience – guests have shared our downs as well as ups as we have theirs. We were passionate about breathing new life into this once sad and neglected place and we attracted guests who understood that passion and were looking for that shared experience.
The place is far from perfect and so are we. That’s what makes it all so interesting. 148 windows and an acre of roof take some upkeep. But some of our renovation decisions have led to us retaining original features rather than replacing them with new because we want the history of the building to sing – even if it is slightly off-key sometimes.
Over a quarter of a decade on we have many more bedrooms – all on a rolling redecoration programme – but the ethos hasn’t changed. We have worked hard to retain the essence of a shared country house experience.
We seek to share the simple joys of country life with our guests  – other places can offer contrived luxury and simpering service much better than we ever could  or would wish to – and simple joys have to be kept simple to stay real.
That experience is borne of genuine hospitality made of genuine interactions. What makes us different are not our facilities but the relationships you will have while you are here – between you and us, you and our staff (whose friendliness we value far more than efficiency) and, most importantly, you and your fellow guests which we hope create longer lasting memories than a loose corner of wallpaper, a chip in the paintwork or a missing jam pot at breakfast. We want you to feel you belong here as much as we do.
We have broken down the artificial barriers of a hotel – there is no reception desk to get in the way of our welcome, there is no barrier between you and the kitchen (if you need something and we can do it, we will. If you ask for something we are unable to provide, we will suggest an alternative), and we encourage you to have a drink in the conservatory and enjoy the live edged bar Oliver built.
If that all excites you, (and if you’ve read this far chances are it does) Augill may be just the place you have been searching for.
If you are looking for a place where whispering to your partner is more appealing than meeting other people and making new friends, where everything runs to a timetable and every choice is from a menu and timed to the minute, where quantity of choice is preferable to quality and where the staff are trained to respond with automatic uniformity rather than spontaneous generosity, Augill won’t be for you.
We hope you do choose to visit and we look forward to welcoming you to our happy family home and for those who do make Augill their second home, there are always the books to complete the story!
Simon, Wendy, Oliver & Emily and all our lovely Augill extended family .

Stay In A Castle Near The Lake District | Augill Castle
Skip to content
Stay In A Castle Near The Lake District
By
Alison, Augill Castle
The quiet side of the Lakes: a castle hotel near the Lake District
There is a certain expectation that if you are looking for a stay  near the Lake District, you need to be right in the middle of it all. Somewhere overlooking a lake, perhaps, or tucked into one of the better-known towns, with walkers in boots passing the window and plenty of places to eat, drink and explore within easy reach.
And, of course, there is nothing wrong with that.
But what if you could spend your days exploring the Lake District and then come back to somewhere altogether quieter? Somewhere with fields rather than crowds outside the window, a little more space, and a castle at the end of the drive?
That is where Augill Castle comes in.
Just around 40 minutes east of the Lake District, Augill sits in the Eden Valley , surrounded by the sort of open Cumbrian countryside that makes you slow down without really meaning to. It is close enough to make exploring the Lake District part of your stay, but far enough away that you can leave the busy bits behind when the day is done.
A quieter place to stay near the Lake District
We love the Lake District, but we also know that it can get busy, particularly when the weather is doing its very best to persuade everyone in the country to head for the hills.
Staying near the Lake District rather than directly in one of its busiest centres gives you a slightly different kind of break. You can still head west for a day of mountain scenery, lakeside walks and those views that make you stop the car just to look at them, but you are not committed to spending your entire holiday navigating busy roads and crowded car parks.
Instead, you can have the best of both.
Spend the day exploring, then head back towards the quieter side of Cumbria, where the landscape opens out and the pace feels a little different.
That is one of the things we rather like about being a  castle hotel near the Lake District. You get to enjoy the Lakes, without necessarily having to stay amongst the busiest parts of them.
40 minutes from the Lake District, and a world away
Augill Castle is in the Eden Valley, on the eastern side of Cumbria and close to The Yorkshire Dales , which puts us in a particularly useful spot for anyone wanting to explore more than just one part of the county.
You can head towards the Lake District for the day, but you can also discover the countryside on this side of the county, with its villages, valleys, walking routes and wonderfully quiet roads.
There is something rather lovely about having a destination to come back to after a day out.
You might have spent the morning walking in the Lakes, stopped somewhere for lunch, explored a village or two and taken far too many photographs of stunning mountains reflected in water. By the time you return to Augill, the day s adventure can give way to a slower evening, whether that means dinner, a drink or simply finding a comfortable corner and doing very little at all.
Ullswater
A castle stay near the Lake District that is part of the experience
Augill isn t simply a convenient hotel near the Lake District; the castle is very much part of the reason to come.
It is a proper heritage country house with character, quirks, comfortable rooms and plenty of spaces where you can settle in rather than feeling that you have to keep moving. There are grounds to explore, countryside beyond the gates and the slightly surreal pleasure of being able to say that you are staying in a castle tonight.
It is the kind of place where muddy walking boots don t feel out of place, where children can have space to explore and where you can spend an evening talking about the day s adventures rather than checking what time you need to leave for the next attraction.
In other words, it feels like a stay in its own right.
Exploring the Lake District from Augill
Being near the Lake District means you can easily make the Lakes part of your itinerary, whether you are visiting for the first time or returning to favourite places.
Perhaps you want a proper day out on the Roof of England walk, or perhaps you are more interested in lakeside walks , pretty villages, good food and finding somewhere with a particularly good view for a cup of coffee . There is no right way to do the Lake District, which is rather the point.
And because you are staying just outside the main tourist centres, you have the opportunity to mix things up a little.
One day could be spent exploring the Lake District, while the next might take you along quieter walking routes in the Eden Valley . You could head further north, explore historic market towns such as Appleby, Kirkby Stephen or even as far as Penrith, follow part of a long-distance trail or simply get in the car and see where the road takes you.
You don t have to fill every minute, either.
Sometimes the best Lake District break involves doing considerably less than you planned.
Walking the Lake District
If walking is one of the reasons you are coming to Cumbria, being based near the Lake District gives you plenty of choice.
The famous Lake District fells are within reach, of course, but you don t need to climb a mountain every day to have a good walking holiday. The countryside around Augill offers its own routes, with quiet lanes, open fields and long-distance paths to discover.
For anyone walking sections of the Coast to Coast , Westmorland Way
or other routes through this part of the country, Augill can also make a rather memorable place to stop and recharge.
There is something very satisfying about arriving somewhere after a day on foot, taking off your boots and knowing you don t have to do anything else until morning.
And if your idea of walking involves a gentle wander followed by cake rather than a full day s hike, we are entirely behind that approach too.
Why stay near the Lake District rather than in it?
F
